title: Exotic-car dealers: narrow published-business-contact workflow
hypothesis: The live Maps-first route can identify a published business contact for a genuinely exotic, luxury, or classic-car dealer, but its current broad allowlist also admits ordinary dealers. A listing, published dealership line, dealer-license record, or person named in a filing does not establish an owner-confirmed mobile; delivery requires the implemented contact/compliance gates and independent ownership and handset evidence.
ownerSource: No dealer-specific owner-confirming adapter is implemented. The catalog's NY DMV dealer (DLU) rows are a possible future licensee-candidate source, but this review did not fetch DMV data and the implemented ny_repair_shops adapter explicitly keeps only RS and RSB repair-shop rows.
phoneSource: The implemented recipe-A route begins with the published Maps business number for the exotic-car-dealer keyword. It is a business-contact candidate only until line type, reachability, DNC/TCPA, suppression, duplicate, ownership, and handset evidence are separately satisfied.

workflow.label: Discover published dealer listing
workflow.detail: Use the live recipe-A Maps query. A listing and advertised number are dealership evidence only.

workflow.label: Exotic-dealer fit?
workflow.detail: Require exotic, luxury, or classic-car-dealer evidence. Ordinary used, OEM, rental, repair, parts, detailing, and generic car-dealer results are not sufficient.

workflow.label: Hold broad or adjacent dealer
workflow.detail: Hold a generic dealer or adjacent automotive listing; do not call it exotic solely because the current allowlist matches car dealer.

workflow.label: Independent dealership candidate?
workflow.detail: Hold OEM, franchise, group, and multi-location operators from the owner-candidate branch pending separately reviewed ownership evidence.

workflow.label: Hold OEM, franchise, or group
workflow.detail: A dealership brand or group can retain a business-contact classification but is not owner-confirmed from the listing.

workflow.label: Published business number present?
workflow.detail: The advertised dealership number is not a person number. Do not use a dealer, filing, or business address to discover a private number.

workflow.label: Hold missing contact
workflow.detail: Keep the business identity only when no published business contact exists.

workflow.label: Business-contact gates
workflow.detail: Apply the implemented mobile-line, reachable, DNC/TCPA, suppression, duplicate, and freshness checks. Passing them does not prove ownership.

workflow.label: Hold failed contact gate
workflow.detail: Hold non-mobile, unreachable, DNC/TCPA, suppressed, duplicate, or otherwise unsupported rows.

workflow.label: Independent owner and handset evidence?
workflow.detail: A dealer-license licensee, public filing role, published dealership line, or mobile result alone is insufficient; retain each only as candidate evidence.

workflow.label: Hold as business contact
workflow.detail: Do not label or deliver an owner-confirmed mobile without independently recorded ownership and handset evidence.

workflow.label: Deliver supported contact
workflow.detail: Only a future workflow that records independent ownership and handset evidence plus every contact/compliance gate may use an owner-confirmed classification.

failures.risk: Ordinary used and OEM dealer listings pass the exotic-car-dealer allowlist because its final alternative is car dealer.
failures.mitigation: Remove the generic car dealer alternative and retain only specific exotic/luxury/classic dealer terms; add a five-case regression that rejects used and OEM dealer fixtures.

failures.risk: A published dealership switchboard or mobile line is called a direct owner mobile.
failures.mitigation: Treat it as a published business contact and require mobile, live, DNC/TCPA, suppression, dedupe, independent ownership, and handset evidence before an owner-confirmed label.

failures.risk: A dealer licensee or public filing officer is represented as the current owner, or a business address is used for personal-phone enrichment.
failures.mitigation: Keep license and filing roles as identity-candidate evidence only; prohibit personal-phone and address enrichment, and require independent ownership and handset evidence.

failures.risk: OEM franchises, dealer groups, and multi-location luxury operators are treated as one-owner independent dealers.
failures.mitigation: Hold brand, franchise, group, and multi-location signals before forming an owner hypothesis.

failures.risk: The NY repair-shop adapter is mistaken for a dealer register because the catalog's DMV dataset also has DLU dealer rows.
failures.mitigation: Do not map exotic dealers to ny_repair_shops: its parser filters to RS and RSB. Build and test a dealer-specific DLU adapter only after a separately approved source review.

iterations.hypothesis: The live exotic-car-dealer allowlist distinguishes exotic, luxury, and classic dealers from generic dealership results.
iterations.test: Five-case code audit on 2026-09-24 using the exact RegExp constructed from lead-engine-brain.json industries.exotic_car_dealers.allow in ingestRows: Prestige Exotic Motors — Exotic Car Dealer; Luxury Auto Gallery — Luxury Car Dealer; Heritage Classics — Classic Car Dealer; Value Lane — Used Car Dealer; Metro Ford — Car Dealer. The audit also called route('luxury car dealer', 'NY'). No network, DMV, paid, secret, or contact-data call was made.
iterations.observed: All five strings matched. The first three demonstrate intended inclusion; Value Lane and Metro Ford demonstrate false inclusion caused by the generic car dealer alternative. route('luxury car dealer', 'NY') selected exotic_car_dealers recipe A. This audit measures code behavior only, not listing coverage, line type, reachability, DNC, ownership, handset evidence, or delivery.
iterations.change: Treat generic car dealer as a concrete allowlist defect. Replace the generic alternative with specific exotic/luxury/classic dealer phrases and add the same five fixtures as a regression test; retain used and OEM dealer rows on the hold branch until a reviewed workflow covers them.

iterations.test: Focused synthetic regression checks in tests/lead-engine-industry-corrections.test.ts, lead-engine-reviews.test.ts, lead-engine-gates-jobs.test.ts and lead-engine-jobs.test.ts. No paid provider call.
iterations.observed: A dedicated profile requires exotic/luxury/classic automotive context. Generic used/OEM dealers and luxury-spa counterexamples fail before verification even though the historical broad brain allow field remains unchanged.
iterations.change: Shared runtime correction integrated. Original source samples are retained with their original denominators; no phone-yield improvement is claimed.

measurement.result: Exact live allowlist audit: exotic, luxury, classic, used, and OEM dealer strings all matched because the pattern ends in car dealer. The NY luxury-car-dealer route selected recipe A. Code audit only; no live source, DMV, phone, identity, ownership, handset, compliance, or delivery measurement.

cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. The historical Anas brain rate has a different denominator and is not a per-clean cost for this workflow.

implementation.summary: A dedicated profile requires exotic/luxury/classic automotive context. Generic used/OEM dealers and luxury-spa counterexamples fail before verification even though the historical broad brain allow field remains unchanged. Original review: The industry is recognized and runs the recipe-A Maps route with existing business-contact and delivery gates. It has no dealer-specific owner-confirming adapter, and its current allowlist overadmits ordinary dealers. The NY repair adapter does not cover DLU dealer rows.

nextMeasurement: After the allowlist correction, run the same five synthetic discovery fixtures through ingestRows and verify that specific exotic/luxury/classic dealer cases proceed while generic used and OEM dealer cases are filtered. A later authorized outcome pilot must separately measure published-contact line type, DNC/TCPA, reachability, reached owner, independent ownership evidence, handset evidence, and delivery; do not query DMV or use business addresses for personal-phone discovery.
